blocks.text: On Wednesday night, July 23, 2025, the public's attention in Indonesia was on a private data protection issue after reports showed that the government had committed allowing overseas transfer, including to the US, as part of its attempt to remove digital trade barriers, services and investments, as the White House announced.
This step, which includes the legal certainty to transfer data to the US to meet the terms of the Joint Initiative on Services Domestic Regulation on WTO, triggers controversy.
The privacy and civil society activists are asking whether the public's data is pawned for economic interest and diplomacy.
Critics underline the risk of privacy violations, especially with no comprehensive personal data protection laws in Indonesia.
They're worried data could be exploited by foreign parties or corporations without the knowledge of its owner.

The government hasn't responded in detail, although it seems to be trying to balance the economy and protection data in the WTO context. The public is awaiting strong regulation to maintain privacy rights.
This issue reflects a global challenge in the digital age, where data sovereignty is becoming hazy.
While economic opportunities are open, the government has to make sure the public data doesn't become a victim of international negotiations, with open dialogue and solid regulation as a key.
